question: Explain how the unidirectional conduction property of a semiconductor diode can be related to switching action in digital electronics.

options.A: A diode behaves as a closed switch in both forward and reverse bias, so it cannot represent two logic states.
options.B: A diode behaves as an open switch in forward bias and as a closed switch in reverse bias, so logic states are reversed.
options.C: A diode is useful in digital electronics only because it amplifies current in both directions.
options.D:
Forward bias
A diode conducts and behaves nearly as a closed switch.
Reverse bias
It blocks current and behaves nearly as an open switch. These two states can represent logic levels such as logic $1$ and logic $0$ in simple switching circuits.
